rows.14:13160:
{f:I|I} wrapped my hands around the doll's neck.
Then I yanked with all my strength.{p}
rows.14:131c4: With a wet, sucking pop, the doll's head tore free.{p}
rows.14:13208:
"Kiiiiiiieee!"
The doll let out an anguished shriek, and then it stopped moving.
A spinal cord, just like a human's, had come slithering out with the head I'd yanked off.
And it was still twitching.
The yellow-green slime that had coated the doll's surface melted and ran down {f:my|my} shoulders.
Something like human nerves was stuck fast to my skin.{p}
rows.14:1333c:
{f:I|I} grabbed a fistful of the sand beside me, all that was left of the principal.
Then I hurled it straight at the face of the doll that was strangling {f:me|me}.{p}
rows.14:13510:
I already heard what Fukuzawa had to say a little while ago{f:.|.}
I'll try someone else.{p}
rows.14:13554:
No, wait, wasn't Iwashita absent today?
I was wandering aimlessly, thinking that, when Iwashita appeared right in front of me.{p}
rows.14:135e4:
(Whoa...)
I almost cried out, but I just barely held it in.
"I'm sorry about yesterday."
"Oh, Iwashita..."
She was a different person now, bright and cheerful.
"What's the matter? You look so gloomy."
"...Weren't you supposed to be absent today...?"
I said it with my feelings held in check.
I just couldn't forget the way she'd acted yesterday.{p}
rows.14:137a0:
"What are you talking about, {a}?"
The Iwashita in front of me now acted as if yesterday had never happened.
"That Arai guy was never supposed to come, you know."
I said it a little too heatedly.
"Well, what does it matter? We were short a member anyway..."
Then I briefly told Iwashita what had happened after she went home yesterday.
"I see. All right. Then I'll help you look for him."{p}
rows.14:13990:
I was getting desperate.
After hearing that story, I'd seen something eerie, something I couldn't explain.
If Arai's story was true, this year's sacrifice might be me.
Arai wasn't supposed to come. So why had he shown up at the newspaper club uninvited and told that story?
Could it be that he came to warn me about the sacrifice...?{p}
rows.14:13adc:
We went around every one of the second-year classrooms.
And we learned one fact.{p}
rows.14:13b30:
There was nobody named Shoji Arai in the second year.
Then who was he?
We had to be overlooking something.
Whatever it took, we had to find out for sure.
"{a}!"
Just as we were about to make another round of the second-year classrooms, a voice called out to us from behind.{p}
rows.14:13c2c:
"Shindo!"
I turned around, and there stood Shindo.
"Iwashita and {a} hanging out together? That's weird.
What brought this on?"
"That's none of your business."
"No, we just came looking for Arai, that's all."
"You looking for Arai so you can beat the crap out of him too?"
I hadn't been planning to beat him up or anything, but I'd come looking for him, same as Shindo.
Shindo had a tense look on his face.
He looked a little pale, too.{p}
rows.14:13dec:
He came over to me and muttered with a sigh.
"...So, how'd it go? You find Arai?"
He asked it with a serious face.
(Shindo too...?
Shindo couldn't find him either?)
I honestly shook my head.
"...Figures. C'mere a sec."
He grabbed my sleeve and dragged me off.{p}
rows.14:13f14: "What is it? You'll let me in on it too, won't you?"{p}
rows.14:13f4c:
Shindo led me into the shadow of a pillar.
Then he started talking in a low voice.
It seemed to be something it would be bad for anyone to overhear.
"Looks like there's no such guy as Shoji Arai in the second year at our school."
Shindo's words completely crushed my faint hope.
"...Yesterday, after all that, it was bugging me, so I looked into a bunch of stuff.
And guess what.
That doll story he told looks like it might actually be true.
Every single year, at least one person ends up as the victim and dies.{p}
rows.14:140e4:
I went looking for Arai to beat the truth out of him, but there's no guy like that among our students.
I can't stop thinking about the last thing he said.
One of us is gonna be this year's sacrifice.
And the guy who said that doesn't even exist in this world. Doesn't that creep you out?{p}
rows.14:141e8:
...Hey, {a}.
You listening to me?"
Shindo poked me in the arm.
I was listening.
But my eyes were glued to Iwashita.{p}
rows.14:14290:
She was staring at the corner of the hallway, frightened.
What was wrong with her?
What was she looking at?
Warily, I followed her gaze.{p}
rows.14:1433c:
"Arai..."
"Huh? What is it, {a}?"
Shindo turned around and shouted.
"Arai!"
He went running toward Arai.
Iwashita and I chased after him.
But Arai's silhouette disappeared around the corner before we got there.{p}
rows.14:14424:
When we rounded the corner, Arai was nowhere to be seen.
"Where the hell did Arai go?"
Shindo muttered, out of breath.
"He's a student at this school.
If he's not a second-year, then is he a first-year? A third-year?"
When he said that, Iwashita cut in.{p}
rows.14:14518:
"Couldn't it be a fake name?"
"Yeah... With how many kids go here, it'd take forever to check them all."
"If I remember correctly, the library keeps photographs taken at school events, doesn't it?"
I just listened to the two of them talk, dazed.
"Oh, right. Let's go."
When Shindo said that, we headed for the library.{p}
rows.14:14654:
"I believe they're here."
When we got to the library, we searched for the albums with Iwashita showing the way.
"Oh, here they are."
I found the albums and called everyone over.{p}
rows.14:146ec:
But we couldn't find Arai anywhere in those albums.
"We all saw him just now, right?"
Shindo said it in a voice that was half bewildered, half angry.
We'd hit a dead end.
And we could feel that we had wandered into an eerie maze with no way back out.
For the time being, we split up.{p}
rows.14:14834:
The next day, when I went to school, I learned that Hosoda was dead.
(Why did he die?)
They said the cause of death was a heart attack on his way home, but that wasn't what I wanted to know.
Was he this year's victim...?{p}
rows.14:14ac4:
Neither the ambulance nor the police had arrived yet.
Shindo spoke, almost in a mutter.{p}
rows.14:14b14:
"Two of the people from that meeting are dead.
That leaves me, you, Iwashita, Kazama, and Arai.
But Arai's not at this school."
He had the face of someone holding back terror.
"I figured Hosoda was this year's victim..."
Shindo murmured it under his breath.
We didn't know what we should do, and for a while we just stood there, frozen.{p}
rows.14:14cd4:
...I parted ways with Shindo.
The next day, just as I'd feared, Kazama had been killed.
I couldn't even be surprised anymore.
Maybe everyone from that day was going to die like this, one by one.
But why...?{p}
rows.14:14dac:
After school, the three of us got together.
But none of us could bring ourselves to speak.
Next, one of us here would...
I thought it, but I couldn't say it out loud.
But the others had to be thinking the same thing.
"The only lead we've got is the principal."
Shindo said.
That's right.
If we looked into the principal, we might find something out.
"Let's go."
I looked from one of them to the other.{p}
rows.14:14f08:
Now that we'd been driven this far into a corner, we couldn't be picky about how we did it.
We made sure there was no one in the hallway outside the principal's office, then crept up to it.{p}
rows.14:14fa0:
The principal's office wasn't locked.
We decided to split up and search for clues.
The desk, the shelves, the walls... we checked everything.
...How long had we been at it?{p}
rows.14:15054:
"Nothing! There's nothing here!"
Shindo suddenly spat out.
He was right. There was nothing that seemed to have anything to do with all this.
What were we supposed to do?
For a while, we just stood there, stunned.{p}
rows.14:15108: Just then, we heard a window swing open with a clack.{p}
rows.14:1514c:
"Hello there, you three."
Before we knew it, Arai was standing there.
Then the door of the principal's office opened, and a whole group of teachers came in.
All of them had vacant eyes.
"...Kill the three of them."
At Arai's word, the teachers closed in on us like puppets.
Were we going to be killed?
No... Arai had said it himself, back then, hadn't he?
That only one more would become the doll's sacrifice.
Then why did so many people have to be killed?
I'll never know now.
Not me, when I'm about to die...{p}
rows.14:15324:
Forget it. If I went to see that person now, it'd only put me in a bad mood{f:.|.}
I'll try someone else.{p}
rows.14:15380:
Right, there was nobody in that classroom earlier.
It looks like everyone's already gone home, so I'll try someone else{f:.|.}{p}
rows.14:153f0:
No, I never want to go see Kazama again.
It'd be smarter to try someone else.{p}
rows.14:154d0:
I'm not going near him again.
Best friends? You've got to be kidding me.{p}
rows.14:15614:
{f:I|I} ran down the stairs and chased after Kiyose.
I made it as far as the entrance to the old school building{f:, but|, but} Kiyose was nowhere around.
"Maybe he went inside."
{f:I|I} went in.{p}
rows.14:156d8:
Inside, it was dead silent, with no sign of anyone.
"Maybe he's not in here after all{f:.|.}"{p}
rows.14:1574c:
With that thought, I went back outside, and from inside the old school building came a man's faint scream.
Kiyose...?
{f:I|I} slowly made my way toward the scream.
It was this way, {f:I think|wasn't it}...
Thinking that, I climbed the stairs.{p}
rows.14:15830:
Everything around me had gone quiet again.
{f:I|I} peered into a second-floor classroom.{p}
rows.14:15888:
"Ah, Arai..."
Arai was standing there.
"What are you trying to dig up?"
He glared hard at {f:me|me}.
Somehow, he had a different air about him than the Arai of yesterday.
The way he talked was strange too{f:.|.}
For an instant, Arai dropped his gaze to the floor.{p}
rows.14:1597c: I looked, and there was Kiyose, lying face down.{p}
rows.14:159c0:
Blood was spreading out around Kiyose's head.
"This guy knew what I really am.
So I killed him.
I wouldn't want anyone interfering with the sacrificial ritual, you see."
He was holding a bloody knife.
{f:My|My} hands were clammy with tension, and I couldn't move.{p}
rows.14:15ad0:
"You've realized by now that I'm not a student at this school, haven't you?"
Arai came closer, step by step.
All {f:I|I} could manage was a nod.
"But that's not quite accurate.
To be precise, I used to be a student here.
But I lost my body in a certain accident."{p}
rows.14:15bdc:
Wrapped in a shimmering light like a heat haze, his body changed into a doll.
"And only my soul came to dwell in a doll, so I barely managed to stay in this world.
But after today, that's over.
The last victim is you, {a}{f:|}.
Once you take my place, I'll come back to life as a complete human being.
But relax.
Unlike the ones before you, you get to stay in this world as a doll.
If you put your mind to it, you can come back to life like me."
From Arai, now in the form of a doll, spread a shadow like some eerie demon.
That was the last thing {f:I|I} saw as a human being.{p}
rows.14:15df4:
......When I came to, there was a classroom spread out before my eyes.
(Huh... I'm alive?){p}
rows.14:15f0c:
The glass shattered with a tremendous crash.
Someone might come running.
For a while, {f:I|I} braced myself.
...There was no sign of anyone coming.{p}
rows.14:16168:
Huh, something's stuck on here...
In the corner of the shelf, a sheet of paper with something like an incantation written on it had been pasted.{p}
rows.14:161d8:
I peeled it off and took a good look{f:, but|, but} I couldn't tell what it was.
What on earth is going on{f:?|?}{p}
rows.14:16260:
After making sure there was nothing in the shelf, I went over to the principal's desk.
There had to be some clue...
{f:I|I} yanked open every drawer, one after another.
Only the top right drawer was locked.{p}
rows.14:16318: Without a thought for the consequences, {f:I|I} pried it open by force with whatever was lying around.{p}
rows.14:1637c:
...Inside were a diary and a battered old Western book.
"What {f:the hell|on earth} is this?"
The Western book was nothing {f:I|I} could possibly read.
{f:I|I} decided to read the diary.
There was a strap buckled around the diary{f:, but|, but} I cut it with the scissors on the desk and opened it.
It was less a diary than a logbook.
Records of the students who had been sacrificed, going back years, and the plans for them{f:.|.}
According to the diary, the sacrifices had been offered for the glory of the sports clubs.
"For something like this..."
{f:I|I} kept on reading.{p}
rows.14:16670:
The principal was standing there.
"Principal..."
"Uoooooooh☆"
The principal let out a roar like a beast and raised a golf club over his head.
What {f:the hell|on earth}...★
Whatever it was, I had to get away somewhere!{p}
rows.14:16744:
The golf club smashed the shelf to pieces.
Having barely dodged it, {f:I|I} ducked around behind the desk.{p}
rows.14:167e8:
I followed the principal's gaze down to {f:my|my} fist and saw I was clutching the paper I'd peeled off earlier with all my might.
(Could it be... this paper...?){p}
rows.14:16874: {f:I|I} ripped the paper apart and threw it away.{p}
rows.14:16958:
What on earth is this...?
The darkness engulfed the principal's body.
"I'm sorry... I'm so sor..."
He was apologizing, writhing in agony inside the darkness.
The principal screamed and collapsed to the floor.
Then the darkness took the shapes of many people's bodies and faded away.{p}
rows.14:16af0: On the way home, I kept thinking that those shadows might have been the students who had been sacrificed all these years.{p}
rows.14:16be4:
...No way.
{f:Has|Has} the doll's evil hand reached this new principal too?{p}
rows.14:16d30:
I'm never going near him again.
Best friends? You've got to be kidding me.
But why is he so hung up on being best friends, anyway?
I just started walking, with nowhere in particular to go.{p}
